summary: Front and rear range lights, lit in 1883, that guided ships into Bouctouche Harbour. The front tower of 1916 stands on residential land; the rear tower came down in 2022.

light.characteristic: fixed white (since 26 September 1903; fixed white catoptric in 1883)
light.note: Front light visible 10 nm from 1903; back light 12 nm (1883 and 1903 figures)

structures.type: skeletal tower with enclosed upper portion
structures.note: Type disputed: LighthouseFriends gives a skeletal tower 44.6 ft (13.6 m) with an enclosed upper section; the Lighthouse Directory gives a 13 m (44 ft) square pyramidal wood tower with gallery and lantern. Removal: LighthouseFriends says demolished 2022; the Lighthouse Directory says removed by helicopter 2022.

access.note: Register: surrounded entirely by a residential property. LighthouseFriends: grounds open, tower closed.

events.note: Two range lights (front and back) established on Church or Indian Point
Front light changed from red to white on 26 September 1903; back light mast raised 10 ft

notes_for_editor: 1) KEEPER START DATE, disputed. LighthouseFriends gives 1883. The Department's keeper list for the year ended 30 June 1900 gives a Maillet at Indian Point, Buctouche, appointed 7 July 1888 (archive.org 1901v35i9p21_0025, scan p. 225, printed p. 128). The page image was opened in the browser and the row reads 'Maillet, D. O.', 'Indian Point, Buctouche', 'July 7, 1888' on one line, so the row alignment is confirmed. The same name at the same station also appears in the Department's 1915 keepers' table (archive.org 1916v51i17p21_1196, scan p. 73, printed p. 66), where the OCR reads 'D. O. Maillet ... July 7, 1883'. That line is NOT in the story: the page image could not be read at legible size in the browser, so the 1883 reading is unverified. A human should check that page image before the date is settled. 2) HEIGHT of the front tower: register and Parks 6.3 m (20.6 ft); LighthouseFriends 20.7 ft (2013); the Lighthouse Directory 4 m (14 ft). The story gives the register figure and the Directory's disagreement. 3) REAR TOWER: LighthouseFriends (skeletal, 44.6 ft, enclosed upper section, demolished 2022) and the Lighthouse Directory (13 m square pyramidal wood tower with gallery, lantern and enclosed watch room, removed by helicopter 2022) describe it differently; the story states both. 4) STATUS: the brief's record says active (OSM). The Lighthouse Directory and LighthouseFriends say the range was discontinued and the front light inactive from 2014. The 2022 register entry and the Parks release (2 June 2022) say the light continues to mark the channel. The story says it is disputed. 5) ACCESS: LighthouseFriends and the Lighthouse Directory say grounds open, tower closed; the register says the front tower is surrounded entirely by residential property. The story gives both. 6) The 1883 figures (23 ft towers, catoptric optic, 9 and 12 miles) are LighthouseFriends' quotation of the Department's 1883 report, which is not in the local corpus (it starts in 1900); they are unverified. Miles are kept as printed; the sources do not say statute or nautical. 7) Gerald Maillet (service to 1963, after about 1960) is named only in his public role as keeper and caretaker, as LighthouseFriends prints it, with no personal detail. 8) Several Department entries for 'Indian point' (1906, 1907, 1909) refer to Indian Point, Prince Edward Island, and are excluded. 9) No wrecks, storms or rescues were sourced for this station, so that chapter is omitted. 10) Fact-check pass 2026-10-27: sentences were rewritten where they followed LighthouseFriends' wording too closely (a copyrighted site). The Buctouche bar light (1902) is a different light and is marked as such in the story.
